BERT4Rec explicitly acknowledges the mismatch between random interior reconstruction and future-item prediction; its original recipe includes last-item-only masking and appended-MASK inference. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690). [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) argues that random masking is weakly aligned with recommendation and can increase training time. A relevant 2025 direction, [Masked History Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23649), combines history reconstruction with next-item prediction and progressively shifts emphasis toward prediction; its evidence concerns generative recommenders, not a controlled BERT4Rec terminal-mask diagnostic.

Proposed controlled probe: within the same checkpoint, choose identical training-history targets and compare interior masking with right context against truncated-prefix terminal masking. Always replace the target with reserved MASK; left-pad, read the final nonpadding position for terminal predictions, and prevent shifted-target leakage. Measure per-target cross-entropy, target-minus-hardest-negative score margin, and paired rank changes using identical candidates. Stratify by prefix length and training-only target-frequency bins; include frequency-matched negatives and report both within-bin and macro results. This separates target popularity from context availability, although truncation also changes context length and position.

For gradient agreement, compute terminal and interior loss gradients on the same parameters with dropout disabled, reporting cosine similarity, gradient norms, and fraction of negative dot products, separately for backbone and embeddings. [Gradient Surgery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782) motivates conflicting-gradient analysis; applying it here is a proposed diagnostic, not an established BERT4Rec result. Negative cosine indicates local objective conflict, not proof of worse validation ranking. Test masking-weight changes within one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category; select using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
